$schema-note: Deterministic asset budgets for issue #33. All limits are RAW bytes (uncompressed file size) measured from the production `astro build` output by web/tests/build/asset-budgets.test.ts. Raw bytes are gated because, for a given source tree, they are identical on any machine -- no compressor, so no zlib/brotli version variance. (Two pages, home and compare, stamp the build date via `new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)`, a fixed-width 10-char field: its byte LENGTH is stable across days even though its content is not, so the budgeted number does not move with the calendar.) gzip and brotli are reported by `npm run assets:report` for realism but never gated. There is no override, skip or force flag; an intentional exception is an explicit entry here with a stated reason, which is reviewable, never a bypass.
headroom-note: Ceilings sit ~12-26% above the value measured when they were set, leaving room for normal catalog growth while still reddening on a real regression -- and because a raw-byte budget is a claim about the whole built tree, it goes stale on any markup or data change by anyone, which no file-collision check can detect. The measured baseline for each entry is recorded in `measuredRaw` so the headroom is auditable. The ceilings were raised (home, catalog, updates, providers) for three causes measured earlier: the BASE_PATH=/ModelTree/ pin (+380..+5449 per route, the deploy prefix CI applies that a local root build did not), #634's SEO head markup (canonical, robots, 9 Open Graph + 5 Twitter tags, small inline JSON-LD, on every route), and #647's variant-positioning dataset plus expanded LineageExplorer/ModelPassport inlining more per-model tier data. Re-baselined on 2026-08-31 against trunk 7c506bd1 (the current rebased merge-base). Two prior re-baselines are folded into the measured values: #665 (long-tail family depth, +728..+7790 HTML) and then the 7-commit span 356989e9..7c506bd1, whose only structural mover is #674 (render EVERY cited source for a variant-positioning record, not just the first): #674 added ~16 lines to global.css (+117 raw CSS on every route, since the stylesheet is shared) and multi-source HTML to the lineage/variant routes (home +1472, tree/compare +617 each; providers +280 incl. a +165 shared-JS re-chunk from LineageExplorer.tsx). #675 nudged providers/[slug].astro (+4 lines, net ~0). The five data/test-only commits (#668/#671/#673/#676/#680) net near-zero rendered bytes. Every one of these was absorbed within existing headroom, so NO ceiling changed on this re-baseline and each `reason` records where the growth landed.
drift-note: RE-BASELINED 2026-09-02 for #813 against this branch merged with trunk 8e8ae6f9, which is the state CI builds for a pull request and the state `main` holds after the merge -- so every `measuredRaw` below is the figure that build actually produces. It was not before: the recorded values had been left at their 2026-08-31 baseline while 23 commits of data and markup landed on top, so EVERY route's recorded figure understated the truth -- tree by 75,608 bytes (677,003 recorded against 752,611 measured, 11.2%), home by 46,854, catalog by 28,502, benchmarks by 17,969, compare by 22,791, updates by 12,378, the worst passport page by 7,591 and the worst provider page by 5,837. No ceiling was ever breached, so nothing failed; `measuredRaw` is documentation, not enforcement, and the test asserts `criticalMaxRaw`. That is precisely why the drift was expensive rather than harmless -- it caused no red build and it quietly told anyone sizing a change that /tree had 82,997 bytes to spend when it had 7,389, which is what made a fully-researched data tranche look unaffordable (#811). Documentation that no test reads is documentation that decays, so `measuredDrift` below is now checked: asset-budgets.test.ts asserts every recorded measurement stays within `maxFraction` of the build's real figure, and a data tranche that outgrows it must re-run `npm run assets:report` and re-record these numbers rather than let them rot. That is a tightening and never a bypass -- the ceilings are untouched and still enforced exactly as before.

measuredDrift.reason: How far a recorded `measuredRaw`/`measuredWorst*`/`*MeasuredRaw` may sit from the figure the production build actually produces before the test reddens. 2% is chosen against the drift it exists to catch, not picked round: the 2026-09-02 re-baseline found the eight recorded figures 0.93% to 11.17% stale, and a 5% tolerance would have caught exactly ONE of them (tree, 11.17%) while home (4.83%), catalog (4.92%), the worst passport page (4.66%), benchmarks (4.04%), compare (3.13%) and updates (2.89%) all rotted on unnoticed -- six of the eight, including the two whose staleness misled #811. 2% catches seven of the eight; only the worst provider page (0.93%) sits under it, and a figure that close is not yet lying about what a change can afford. The tolerance is a FRACTION OF THE RECORDED VALUE with no absolute floor, so `measuredWorstJsRaw: 0` means exactly 0: that entry is the static-hydration tripwire and a page that starts shipping any island JS should have to say so here, over and above the separate `jsMaxRaw` ceiling. Raw bytes are deterministic for a given source tree (see the $schema-note), so this cannot flake; a failure always means the recorded number is wrong and re-recording it is the fix. Re-record with `npm run assets:report`. This guard never permits more bytes -- exceeding a ceiling still fails on the ceiling.

fixedRoutes.reason: Homepage carries the largest HTML (search index inlined into island props) plus the search and lineage islands. Ceiling raised from 900000 for #647 inlining variant-positioning tier data into the home search/lineage index (HTML +195k), with #634 head markup and the BASE_PATH pin (+5449) on top; #665 then added +7066 of long-tail family HTML, and #674 (render every cited source) added +1472 more (HTML +1190, shared css +117, shared js +165), all absorbed. Re-measured 1016141 at 8e8ae6f9 (#813): the recorded 969287 was 46854 stale, grown by the data landing since 2026-08-31, and absorbed by headroom -- ceiling unchanged. 687 of that is #816's two rewritten `featuredRationale` sentences, which this route pays for because it inlines whole records into island props the way /tree did before #813 projected them -- so it is the obvious next candidate if breadth ever presses on 1105000, and it is NOT changed here, because #813's scope is /tree. +8.7% headroom.

Ceiling raised from 575000 for #647 tier data in the inlined model listing (HTML +92k), with the BASE_PATH pin (+2368) on top; #665 then added +4574 of long-tail family HTML, and #674 added +119 (essentially just the shared css +117; the catalog listing does not expand per-source), all absorbed. Re-measured 608259 at 8e8ae6f9 (#813): the recorded 579757 was 28502 stale, absorbed by headroom -- ceiling unchanged. +7.8% headroom for catalog growth.

Benchmark evidence explorer (#23). Ceiling unchanged: #634 head markup + BASE_PATH pin + #665's +2782 of long-tail family HTML + #674's +115 (shared css +117, HTML net ~0), all absorbed by headroom. Re-measured 463101 at 8e8ae6f9 (#813): the recorded 445132 was 17969 stale, absorbed by headroom -- ceiling unchanged. +12.3% headroom.

Full lineage tree with the ModelTreeExplorer island. Ceiling unchanged and never raised. #813 cut this route by 220029 raw bytes, all of it HTML (447614 -> 227585), by projecting the island props: tree.astro passed whole Organization/ModelFamily/ModelRelease records into a client:load prop, and Astro serialises a prop into an HTML attribute, so every recorded field the components never render was shipped -- and shipped at roughly 1.37x its JSON size, because the wire form tags every scalar as [0,"x"] (27008 B) and attribute escaping turns each of 19586 quotes into " (97930 B). `projectModelTree` now sends the ten release fields, two family fields and two organization fields the explorer and drawer actually read. The server-rendered markup is byte-identical either way (82689 B before and after), which is the evidence that nothing on the surface changed. Before #813 this route measured 752381 at 9e60e48a and 752611 at 8e8ae6f9 -- 7389 spare against 760000, 99.0% consumed, under one further creator of headroom, which is what made a researched data tranche unaffordable (#811). Re-measured 532352 on this branch merged with 8e8ae6f9. That figure is identical with and without #816, which is the projection working as designed rather than a coincidence: #816 rewrote two `featuredRationale` sentences and cost trunk's /tree 230 raw bytes, because the field was among the 24 `featuredRationale` values shipped into the island prop; it is not one of the fields the surface renders, so after projection it is not shipped and prose edits to it now cost this route exactly 0. +42.8% headroom, ~99 further single-family creators at the post-change median cost of 2281 B.

globals.reason: Whole-build ceilings across _astro/. jsTotal/cssTotal catch shared-bundle and shared-stylesheet growth that no single route surfaces. fontTotal is held tight (+12%) so a new font weight or subset is caught. astroDir is the backstop on total hashed-asset weight. Ceilings sized for #647 (js 424190 -> 435805 component code +11.6k; css 101814 -> 103272 global.css +1.5k; dir 713040 -> 726113), each absorbed by headroom. #665 was a pure data/HTML change that added no _astro weight. On the 7c506bd1 re-baseline #674 (render every cited source) added the first _astro movement since: js 435805 -> 435970 (+165, LineageExplorer.tsx/ModelPassport.tsx re-chunk), css 103272 -> 103389 (+117, its ~16 global.css lines), dir 726113 -> 726395 (+282); font unchanged at 187036. Re-measured at 8e8ae6f9 (#813): js 438849, css 104980, font 187036, dir 730865. #813 moved none of these -- it is a page-payload change, so its 220029 bytes came out of tree/index.html and not out of any hashed asset, and the four figures here are identical before and after it. Each absorbed by headroom, no ceiling raised. jsTotal deliberately stays 520000 so it doubles as the NODE_ENV backstop: a dev-React build measures ~670510 raw JS and trips it regardless of the marker assertion. A classifier drift that zeroed a kind is caught by the separate per-kind non-emptiness floor in the test, not by these ceilings.

excludedFromRouteTotals.reason: Issue #34 adds a single static Open Graph card referenced only by an `og:image` tag. Social scrapers fetch it; a visitor on a route never does. The accounting only sums a route's render/hydration resources (stylesheets, island JS,

Generated catalog index endpoint referenced by no route's HTML, so it is never part of a visitor's per-route transfer. Kept out of route totals; whether it has a live consumer is tracked as a follow-up, not decided here.
